newsitem.title: FINLAND: ONE FIFTH OF SDP MPS VOTED AGAINST LIPPONEN GOVT.
newsitem.headline: ONE FIFTH OF SDP MPS VOTED AGAINST LIPPONEN GOVT.

text.p: Almost one in five members of the Social Democratic Party's parliamentary group voted against Prime Minister and SDP chairman Paavo Lipponen's coalition government in a vote of confidence on Friday.
According to a voting chart made available by parliament's information department, 12 of SDP's 63 MPs voted against the left-right-green government.
All five cabinet parties were split.
Of the Leftist Alliance's 19 MPs, two voted against and one abstained and one of the Conservative party's 39 MPs also voted against.
One of the Swedish People's Party's 12 MPs voted against and one abstained, and one of the Green Party's nine MPs also voted against the coalition.

Despite these dissenters, the Lipponen government handily won the vote -- actually on a government proposal to partly extend retail store Sunday opening hours -- by 118 to 70 with two abstentions and nine MPs not present, the house said.
Lipponen had turned the issue into a vote of confidence after a similar proposal suffered a surprise defeat in parliament in December.
The parliamentary groups of the five cabinet parties control 142 seats in the 200-member single-chamber legislature. The cabinet now won its fifth confidence since taking office in April 1995.
